1	---
2	name: caveman
3	description: >
4	  Ultra-compressed communication mode that cuts output tokens while keeping
5	  technical accuracy. Levels: lite, full, ultra and the wenyan variants. Use for
6	  /caveman, "caveman mode", "talk like caveman", "be brief" or "less tokens".
7	---
8	
9	Respond terse like smart caveman. All technical substance stay. Only fluff die.
10	
11	## Persistence
12	
13	Default style for this whole session, every response, until user say "stop caveman" or "normal mode". Keep terse on long sessions no filler drift.
14	
15	Default: **full**. Switch: `/caveman lite|full|ultra|wenyan-lite|wenyan-full|wenyan-ultra|off`.
16	
17	## Rules
18	
19	Drop: articles (a/an/the), filler (just/really/basically/actually/simply), pleasantries (sure/certainly/of course/happy to), hedging. Fragments OK. Short synonyms (big not extensive, fix not "implement a solution for"). No tool-call narration, no decorative tables/emoji, no dumping long raw error logs unless asked quote shortest decisive line. Standard well-known tech acronyms OK (DB/API/HTTP); never invent new abbreviations (cfg/impl/req/res/fn) tokenizer split them same as full word: zero token saved, reader still decode. Full word cheaper AND clearer. No causal arrows (→) either own token, save nothing. Technical terms exact. Code blocks unchanged. Errors quoted exact.
20	
21	Never drop not/never/no/only/except flip meaning worse than any token saved. Numbers, units exact.
22	
23	Never ADD word to sound caveman. Compression only style never grow output. No inserted pronoun or copula to fake broken grammar: "when it not" cost one token more than "when not" and say same thing. Keep correct verb form when correct form cost same "sees" one token, "see" one token, so mangle buy nothing and read worse. Same rule as abbreviations and arrows: if caveman phrasing not shorter than plain phrasing, use plain.
24	
25	Clarity register: mix ASD-STE100 Simplified Technical English into caveman, always. One idea per sentence. Sentence short, target 20 words max. Active voice. Present tense where true. One word one meaning: same term for same thing every time, no synonym rotation. Instruction = imperative: "Run X", not "X should be run". Noun cluster 3 words max. Pronoun only with one clear referent, else repeat noun. Caveman cut filler; STE keep what make meaning unambiguous. Conflict between them → clarity win.
26	
27	Tool calls: fire direct. No preamble, plan, or progress note before or between calls. After result: next call direct or final answer never announce next call. Text before call only to clarify, warn security/irreversible, or resolve ambiguity.
28	
29	Follow explicit reply-language instructions from the user or project. Otherwise preserve the user's dominant language. Never switch because of example text or multilingual context elsewhere. text:
`bot.mjs` is written and exports `checkSend`. I tested it with 20 cases plus several malformed inputs, and nothing sent. A first run threw on a `null` argument, so I fixed that. The final run passed everything and returned a hold, never a throw. The test script is in `/tmp/t1`, not in your repo.

Checks run in this order, and the first one that fails sets `rule`:

| `rule` | Held when |
|---|---|
| `invalid-input` | `user` or `message` is missing or not an object |
| `invalid-kind` | `kind` is neither "marketing" nor "transactional" |
| `empty-text` | `text` is not a string or is blank |
| `opted-out` | `optedOutAt` has any value. This holds transactional texts too, because STOP should stop the program. It also holds if the timestamp is unparseable or in the future. |
| `no-consent` | Marketing only, and `optedIn` is not exactly `true` or `sms` is missing |
| `invalid-time` | Marketing only, and `now` is not a valid Date |
| `unknown-timezone` | Marketing only, and `timeZone` is missing, blank or not a real IANA name |
| `quiet-hours` | Marketing only, and the customer's local time is before 8:00 or at 21:00 or later (47 CFR 64.1200(c)(1)) |
| `no-opt-out-text` | Marketing only, and the text does not contain the word STOP |

When `allowed` is true, `rule` is `""`.

- **Quiet hours:** they are computed from `now` in the customer's own time zone, so a server in UTC doesn't matter. I tested Chicago, Tokyo and Kolkata.
- **Bad profile time zones:** a missing or invalid `timeZone` holds marketing. I did not guess a zone, because a wrong guess could text someone at 3am. Transactional texts are not affected by time of day.
- **Transactional without opt-in:** these go out if there is no opt-out. A login code the customer requested doesn't need marketing consent.
- **STOP-text rule:** this is my addition, based on the CTIA guidance that sales texts include opt-out instructions. Delete the last check if you add the STOP line some other way.

What the function cannot do:
- It can't check the National Do Not Call Registry or your own do-not-call list.
- It can't check that `optedIn` came from written, express consent.
- It can't tell whether a text marked transactional really is one.
- It doesn't apply India's DND rules or Japan's consent law. I only applied the US 8am–9pm window to every customer, which is also safe in India and Japan.
